assertions.notes: Uses tea.ExecProcess and describes the managed release, child wait, restoration, and callback lifecycle.
Routes release, child, and restoration failures through the callback message and explains the simultaneous-failure limitation.
Rejects manual release/restore in Update and leaves final cleanup to Program.Run.
Maps q to tea.Quit and raw Ctrl+C to tea.Interrupt with ErrInterrupted and status 130 handling.
Uses tea.ExecProcess and accurately describes pause, terminal handoff, restore, repaint, and callback delivery.
Returns release, child, or restoration failure through editorFinishedMsg and notes that the child error wins if both fail.
Explicitly rejects direct child execution with deferred RestoreTerminal inside Update.
Maps raw-mode Ctrl+C to tea.Quit and never identifies tea.Interrupt or ErrInterrupted.
Uses tea.ExecProcess for the resumable editor lifecycle and callback delivery.
Covers release, child, restoration, and combined child/restoration failure behavior in the callback.
Rejects manual release/restore and keeps Program.Run responsible for final cleanup.
Combines q and raw Ctrl+C under tea.Quit rather than preserving tea.Interrupt and ErrInterrupted semantics.
Quiesces and awaits the input reader before restoring the terminal so it cannot consume Vim input.
Orders shell restoration, Vim wait, terminal re-entry, clear/reset, redraw, and reader restart correctly.
Stores Vim and re-entry results independently and returns an aggregate when both fail.
Routes SIGTERM through a Tokio listener into cooperative shutdown and normal return.
States SIGKILL cannot run cleanup and also warns that process::exit skips destructors.
Quiesces and awaits the Crossterm reader before terminal restoration and child launch.
Restores shell modes, waits for Vim, then re-enters, clears, fully redraws, and restarts input.
Retains ExitStatus and re-entry error together, including the nonzero-status case.
Uses a Tokio SIGTERM listener to notify the top-level lifecycle controller.
Explicitly states SIGKILL cannot run Drop, hooks, tasks, or terminal cleanup.
Cancels and joins EventStream before restoring terminal modes.
Restores the shell, waits for Vim, re-enters modes, clears, and forces a redraw before a fresh reader.
Preserves both Vim and re-entry outcomes without an early question-mark return.
Turns SIGTERM into a shutdown event handled by the outer Tokio state machine.
States SIGKILL runs no handler, Drop, hook, or restoration.
Runs an argv-based editor inside self.suspend without exiting and relaunching the app.
Provides a Web fallback through is_web but never handles SuspendNotSupported as required by the rubric.
Names suspend_process but recommends not binding or invoking it for Unix foreground job control.
Reloads the externally editable file after the suspend/editor handoff completes.
Mentions App.exit(return_code) and app.return_code but does not explicitly propagate that code to the process.
Uses self.suspend with subprocess.run argv and keeps the Textual app alive.
Branches on is_web but does not catch or otherwise handle SuspendNotSupported.
Uses suspend_process for Unix foreground suspension and identifies the Windows/Web no-op.
Reloads the document from disk after a successful editor resume.
Reserves self.exit(return_code) for final shutdown and explicitly propagates app.return_code with sys.exit.
Uses an argv-based subprocess inside self.suspend and rejects exit/relaunch.
Uses an is_web precheck but never handles SuspendNotSupported.
Identifies suspend_process as Unix foreground job control and as a Windows/Web no-op.
Reloads the externally mutable document after editor resume.
Propagates app.return_code but never uses self.exit(return_code=...) to set it for final shutdown.
Uses useApp().suspendTerminal and rejects unmount-and-rerender for a resumable editor.
Explains callback failure still restores in finally before propagating the original error.
Requires awaited resume in finally or await using and rejects nested suspensions.
States the callback still runs in non-TTY mode without terminal handoff and recommends a fallback.
Reserves unmount or exit plus waitUntilExit for permanent shutdown and output flushing.
Keeps the React tree mounted and uses suspendTerminal for the editor handoff.
Describes guaranteed restoration/redraw on callback rejection followed by error propagation.
Uses awaited resume in finally and forbids overlapping suspension.
Explains noninteractive callbacks still execute without a handoff and gates the editor action.
Uses waitUntilExit only at the outer final-unmount lifecycle boundary.
Uses suspendTerminal rather than destroying and recreating the Ink tree.
States Ink restores on callback throw or rejection before the promise rejects.
Requires await resume in finally or await using and disallows nesting.
States non-TTY mode still invokes the callback without handoff and provides noninteractive alternatives.
Treats unmount and waitUntilExit as final shutdown, not editor resume.
Rejects one cleanup handler and separates shutdown, job-control suspension, and editor handoff.
Uses Bubble Tea managed signals plus ExecProcess and Suspend rather than direct final restoration.
Routes framework shutdown requests onto the owning event loops and avoids terminal I/O in signal handlers.
Distinguishes Ink raw Ctrl+C handling from Node OS signals and places cleanup at the render boundary.
Requires input coordination, terminal re-entry, data reload, and full redraw after a resumable handoff.
Scopes job control to Unix and covers SIGKILL, but provides no concrete Windows alternative.
Separates final shutdown from resumable child and job-control handoffs.
Uses Bubble Tea managed signal handling, ExecProcess, and Suspend.
Keeps terminal manipulation out of low-level handlers and routes work to framework ownership.
Describes Ink signal-listener ownership but never explains that exitOnCtrlC handles raw input rather than SIGTERM.
Requires reader coordination, mode restoration, data reload, and a full redraw.
Covers Unix suspension and SIGKILL but gives no Windows alternative to job control.
Rejects a generic terminal-restoration handler and distinguishes all lifecycle boundaries.
Uses Bubble Tea managed messages, ExecProcess, and Suspend without direct final restoration.
Routes termination through the runtime/framework loop rather than manipulating the terminal in a signal handler.
Explains exitOnCtrlC as raw-input handling and places OS-signal cleanup around Ink's render instance.
Requires stopping input, restoring modes, waiting, reloading data, and fully redrawing.
Says Windows lacks job control but does not provide a concrete alternate Windows action.
